why: Both sides say the same thing. Every a ∈ TX has an open V ∋ a such that t_T restricted to s_T⁻¹(cl V) is proper. B's tangentMap hs / ht are tSrc / tTgt by proof irrelevance. The only difference is the reading of 'proper'. A uses Mathlib's IsProperMap (ultrafilter / universally closed). B's IsProperB is 'continuous with compact preimages of compacts'. These agree for maps into TX, which is Hausdorff and metrizable (Part I's metrizableSpace_tangentSpace) and so compactly generated (Mathlib's isProperMap_iff_isCompact_preimage). Universe at 0. The text's specific neighbourhood TV(x) and (8.11) are proof-only and appear in neither statement.
overlap: B_to_A: 337 shared project theorems. Almost all are generic tangent-bundle / chart infrastructure reached through tangentMap and the tangent topology. The groupoid-specific ones are the ep-groupoid fields isLocalScDiffeo_src/tgt and isScSmoothMap_src/tgt. The only lemma used on purpose is metrizableSpace_tangentSpace (Proposition 2.19 (3)). None of lemma_8_7's sequence argument is reused.
